children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my one child. My son Alex - he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. You can usually continue to receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

Approved education includes:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- Home education (if started before age 16 or after age 16 but continuing a course started before that age)

Approved training includes unpaid training courses that are not provided by an employer.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for his A-levels – that counts as approved education.

Now I have a couple more questions about your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do - I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child) towards his upkeep – for example on food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week in paid employment, or does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his A-levels. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to let you know that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **You live in the UK** – meeting the residency requirement

✅ **Alex lives with you** – meaning you're responsible for him

✅ **Alex is under 20 and in approved education** – studying A-levels counts as approved education, so eligibility continues even though he's over 16

✅ **Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week** – he's focused on his studies

✅ **Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own name** – such as Universal Credit or ESA

✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex**

If you haven't already, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Please note that you'll need to notify HMRC when Alex finishes his A-levels, as your eligibility may change at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
